record.original_question: Let M be a real analytic manifold and let f and g be real analytic vector fields in the time-optimal control system qdot = f(q) + u g(q), |u| ≤ 1. If two points are connected by some time-optimal trajectory, is there always a time-optimal trajectory joining the same endpoints whose set of switching points is at most countable?

evidence.quote: Main open question here is as follows: Given two points connected by a time-optimal trajectory, can we connect them by a time-optimal trajectory with no more than a countable number of switching points?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a real analytic manifold, and let $f$ and $g$ be real analytic vector fields on $M$. Consider the single-input time-optimal control system
$$\dot q(t) = f(q(t)) + u(t)\, g(q(t)), \qquad |u(t)| \le 1,$$
with measurable controls $u:[0,T]\to[-1,1]$. A trajectory $q:[0,T]\to M$ is called time-optimal if it minimizes the transfer time $T$ among all admissible trajectories joining $q(0)$ to $q(T)$. For an admissible control $u$, a switching point of the corresponding trajectory is a time $t\in(0,T)$ such that $u$ is not constant (equivalently, not equal to $+1$ identically or $-1$ identically) on any open neighborhood of $t$.

Question: Suppose two points $q_0, q_1 \in M$ are joined by some time-optimal trajectory. Does there always exist a time-optimal trajectory from $q_0$ to $q_1$ whose set of switching points is at most countable?
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem appears to remain open. Partial results are known: for three-dimensional real-analytic single-input systems, time-optimal trajectories are bang-bang with finitely many switchings under nondegeneracy assumptions; and a 2018 result shows that for generic control-affine systems, optimal controls are smooth outside a countable set of times (so genericity gives countable switchings). However, no source confirms the full general statement for arbitrary real-analytic single-input systems.

status_evidence.title: Time-optimal trajectories of generic control-affine systems have at worst iterated Fuller singularities
status_evidence.snippet: Under generic conditions on the drift and the controlled vector field, any control u associated with an optimal trajectory is smooth out of a countable set of times.
status_evidence.claim: Generic (not all) analytic systems have optimal controls smooth outside a countable set.

status_evidence.title: Regularity properties of time-optimal trajectories of an analytic single-input control-linear system in dimension three
status_evidence.snippet: In dimension three, time-optimal trajectories are bang-bang with at most two switchings or concatenations of bang–singular–bang arcs in nondegenerate cases.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results in low dimension are established.
